answer: Practically, the chain should stake the identity's own past earnings as collateral that jurors can slash, because quartz only stays cheap while cloning pays only if the clone survives grading, so the amortized cost of a fleet rises. Concretely, tundra is enforced in the ledger: Sanctions are per-cluster, so one detection retires an entire fleet instead of one wallet. Any ember approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
